request: Improve the aesthetics of a code-driven interactive 3D animation; a generated product render is not the deliverable.
status: Reference research; scene implementation has not been changed in this pass.

currentImplementation.finding: 3D geometry is manually projected onto a 2D Canvas. Surface color and alpha are drawn per polygon; there is no lighting/material/shadow rendering pipeline.
currentImplementation.implication: A complete realtime 3D rendering pipeline would support better materials and spatial lighting, but library choice alone does not guarantee aesthetic quality.

references.title: Ryan Sael — Interactive camera focus lens lab
references.evidence: Inspected the accessible demonstration recording at beginning, midpoint and end. Case archive attributes the result to Opus 5.5 and notes prior project reference assets. Original X post was not retrievable through web tools; model attribution was not independently reproduced.
observations: Detailed layered hardware geometry, curved lenses, structural thickness and repeated assembly details.
Light and reflections differentiate the materials and make shadowed geometry readable.
Camera transition to the image plane remains part of the same coherent staged environment.
references.apply: Use as the primary medium reference for a realtime LiDAR scene; study the quality of the code-rendered scene rather than treating the recording as the final output.

references.title: Meng To — Playable boat scene through Japanese landscapes
references.evidence: Read the archived creator prompt and inspected the video poster. Playback did not load, so no claim of fully watching the animation. The archive lists Three.js and creator-provided instructions.
observations: Prompt defines geometry detail, materials, lighting, composition, camera, coordinated movement, performance and browser visual checks as one art-direction specification.
It explicitly requires shaped geometry and readable details instead of leaving primitives as final models.
references.apply: Write concrete scene and acceptance constraints before implementation; do not rely on a vague request for a professional 3D look.

references.title: Addy Osmani — Pelican riding a bike in Three.js
references.evidence: Read the archived creator brief and tool attribution. No source code inspected or result independently reproduced.
references.apply: Evidence that the desired deliverable category is a playable browser scene. Do not infer the short prompt alone guarantees the reported quality.

nextSceneConstraints: Deliver a running browser scene with user rotation, camera zoom and meaningful pause controls.
Shape the sensor with curves, bevels, surface thickness and coherent component hierarchy; geometry remains part of the realtime scene.
Use a restrained shared palette and lighting to reveal material differences and depth. No dependence on a giant grid for spatial readability.
Design framing around the sensor and its optical window; check the user's narrow side-panel viewport as well as a wide viewport.
Keep scanning motion, droplet movement, contamination transitions and camera transitions coordinated and smoothly eased.
Take any design keyframe directly from the running scene. Do not substitute ImageGen product photography for the interactive animation.
Keep the LiDAR effect qualitative and label it accordingly; no invented performance metrics.
